Fidelity and stability of an explanation

Source: R/graph-explain.R
explanation_fidelity.Rd

explanation_fidelity() removes the k edges with the largest absolute attribution (\(fid^{+}\), the drop in the explained output; large is good) and, separately, keeps only those k edges (\(fid^{-}\), the drop when everything else is removed; small is good), following Yuan et al. (2022). explanation_stability() reruns an explainer on graphs with small Gaussian feature noise and reports the mean Spearman correlation of edge attributions with the original.

Usage

explanation_fidelity(model, g, explanation, k = 5L)

explanation_stability(
  model,
  g,
  explainer,
  noise = 0.01,
  reps = 5L,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

model

A trained model or graph_fit.

g

A graph_data object.

explanation

A graph_explanation with an edges table.

k

Number of top edges.

explainer

Function (model, g) returning a graph_explanation.

noise

Standard deviation of feature noise.

reps

Number of noisy repetitions.

seed

Optional integer seed.

Value

A named numeric vector.
